International violation? US Army considering hollow point bullets for pistols

Pros: intended target will most likely be terminated. There's almost no chance the bullet will pass through the target and hit an unintended target Con: friendly fire will most likely end up a fatality.

TLDR: Here's the difference between current bullets vs hollow point bullets.

The difference is that while ball ammunition penetrates deeper into an enemy when they are struck, hollow point can break up once they hit an individual, destroying a larger area of tissue and generally producing more damage. As a result, they are more lethal.

The other difference is that, unlike ball ammunition, expanding bullets were banned under the 1899 Hague Convention. The bullets are not used by NATO members, either.
There is a reason expanding bullets were banned for being inhumane. They caused unnecessary damage to tissue.

The US military code (And most military codes) maintain that you should only shoot a person that you intend to kill. Hollow point is used by police forces in many countries for its other benefits, such as vastly reduced risk of hitting bystanders (even a thin wall will remove the killing power).

There's a vast difference between loading hollow point into a machinegun and spraying it at the enemy in the hopes of maiming them, and using hollow point bullets for police work (which is what pistols are used for primarilly in the military).
